title: Apply a water-transfer temporary tattoo
instruction: Apply the water-transfer tattoo inside the marked area on the practice forearm. Remove the backing and leave the image intact.
setup: A cylindrical practice forearm, 200 mm long and 64 mm diameter, covered in smooth PVC vinyl and supported on two rests. A 40 × 35 mm target is marked on its upper surface. A 50 × 60 mm water-transfer backing carries a 35 × 30 mm red heart, image-side down on a 30 × 40 × 30 mm rest, with an unprinted gripping margin. A pre-wetted 40 × 40 × 25 mm cellulose sponge rests in a 70 mm square dish. Both hands start open in the fixed photographed layout; removable waterproof pad covers protect the rig.
scoring: 1.0 if at least 95% of the image transfers inside the target, the backing is fully removed, and both hands have released for three seconds. 0.5 for at least 75% transferred inside the target with the backing removed; 0.25 for at least 50%. Otherwise 0. A torn backing scores 0. Compare a close photograph with the supplied full image and centimetre scale.
fidelity: Native hinged paper and a compliant sponge preserve pickup, pressing and peeling. Transfer requires loaded wet contact, 30 seconds of local wetting and physical backing separation. Short-range wicking, adhesive release and ink deposition are approximated; stiffness and tear limits are uncalibrated. Early peeling loses image regions. No hand attachments or prop-pose edits. Native demo: full score.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 in 1,800 actions; scripted demo: 1.0 in 1,560 actions.
context: A water-transfer tattoo needs even wetting and careful backing removal to leave the picture intact on a curved surface.
reset_notes: Clean and dry the PVC. Use a fresh water-transfer tattoo and a sponge wetted with 5 ml clean water, squeezed until it no longer drips. Qualify the chosen tattoo/PVC pair by one hand application before trials; replace the PVC cover if removal leaves residue. Do not use semi-permanent or dry-rub transfers.
